To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
quantitative maps of fish habitat are useful tools to design spatialized management measures and marine spatial planning with fisheries objectives.

(1) the quantitative mapping of fish habitats may help in designing efficient marine protected area with fisheries objectives, (2) this mapping requires an exhaustive knowledge of environmental descriptors, (3) the habitat models are built using statistical approaches that are robust and validated, (4) the maps are used as input for conservation planning software, (5) this approach is useful for the management of marine living resources and fisheries.
quantitative mapping of essential fish habitats may be used to design MPA networks with fishery objective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantitative mapping of fish habitat, which is a useful tool to design MPA with fishery objectives.
the development of a methodology to quantify the importance of fish habitats and to map their spatial distribution in order to identify and design MPA networks with fishery objective.
the development of habitat models for fish, their implementation in a Geographic Information System and their use for conservation planning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quantitative fish habitat maps are useful tools to design spatialized management measures and MPA with fishery objectives.
the use of habitat suitability models to delineate fish habitats is a powerful and useful tool for designing spatialised management measures, including MPA with fishery objectives.
the quantitative delineation of fish habitats is useful for the design of spatialised management measures, and MPAs with fishery objectives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fish habitat maps may be useful to design efficient and cost-effective MPAs for fisheries.
the quantitative mapping of fish habitats is a useful tool to design efficient and coherent MPA networks with fishery conservation objectives.
the mapping of fish habitat is a useful tool for the design of efficient MPA networks with fishery and conservation objectives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mapping of fish habitats, and in particular of essential fish habitats, is a necessary tool to design spatialized management measures and marine spatial planning.
